rubrics.criterion: Across the network-construction entry points of the pruning pipelines (both the cifar and imagenet trees), no building scope still keeps its layout responsibility and its raw parameter-initialization responsibility fused: at every affected network-setup site, expanding a pruning configuration into layer structure and mutating fresh tensors in place for initialization no longer sit together in one function body, because the two responsibilities now live in separate well-scoped methods or functions.
rubrics.rationale: This instance folded builder and initializer sub-implementations into construction entry bodies across several pipeline components and architecture families; the defining semantic outcome of the task is that every such fused scope has been split back into delegated helpers, whichever helper layout the solver prefers.

rubrics.criterion: The VGG-family construction sites both re-introduce a dedicated feature-stack builder for cfg-driven width layout (the conv/batch-norm stack expansion) and place the raw weight/bias initialization protocol outside that builder, so both the l1-norm-pruning VGG constructor and its lottery-ticket sibling construct identical modules to the folded form.
rubrics.rationale: Both VGG constructors in this case absorbed the same two sub-implementations with different loop idioms; restoring the order-and-width semantics of each is an independently checkable family-level outcome.

rubrics.criterion: The residual-stage construction sites (the cifar l1-norm ResNet with its partial-function shortcut protocol, the imagenet l1-norm ResNet with cursor-walked stage windows, and the weight-level fixed-width ResNet) each delegate stage assembly - including per-stage channel windows, inplanes bookkeeping, and shortcut wiring - to a dedicated helper, with construction results identical to the folded form.
rubrics.rationale: Three distinct residual constructors in three pipeline components were folded with three different assembly idioms; producing one outcome per site (assembly extracted, behavior unchanged) are separate facts about this instance.

rubrics.criterion: The dense-block construction site re-separates dense-unit chaining, growth-rate accumulation, transition compression, and stage attribute creation from raw weight initialization while still producing identical select/mask coupling and transition budgets.
rubrics.rationale: The network-slimming densenet in this case is the deepest folded body (growth arithmetic nested inside stage loops together with initialization); its extraction is a separate measurable outcome.

rubrics.criterion: The module-level slimming VGG factory is re-decomposed so factory orchestration (feature construction, classifier-width recording, initialization gating, optional checkpoint loading) no longer carries raw normalization/fill loops itself: its initialization protocol lives in a scoped implementation of its own while the factory keeps its ordering coupling intact.
rubrics.rationale: This case deliberately included a non-class orchestration site whose gated initialization and optional checkpoint path are interleaved with construction; extracting that machinery without reordering it is an instance-specific capability test.

rubrics.criterion: The reconstructed module trees and their driver-facing surfaces are unchanged by the re-decomposition: module attribute names and registration order (per-stage sequences, feature and classifier stacks, the recorded pruning configuration, select/mask hooks) remain exactly what the pipeline and pruning scripts navigate by name, and constructor signatures that the training drivers call keep accepting the same arguments.
rubrics.rationale: In this repository the pruning drivers address model internals by attribute name and pass construction keyword arguments; every extraction had to preserve those surfaces, which makes surface preservation a required coupled change rather than a style preference.

rubrics.criterion: The sequence of random-number operations during construction is preserved at every site: layer construction, gain/bias filling, and any distribution draws still happen in the same relative order and count, so a seeded build of any affected network yields the same parameter values as before the change.
rubrics.rationale: The folded sites interleave assembly with in-place parameter mutations; the natural cost of a sloppy extraction is a reordered draw sequence that silently changes seeded runs even though shapes and counts still match.

rubrics.criterion: Per-family initialization conventions stay attached to their families: the VGG variants keep their batch-norm gain and bias protocol (including which head layers it touches), and the residual and dense variants keep their own gain conventions and bias handling, rather than being homogenized into one shared initializer that fits only some of them.
rubrics.rationale: This instance's folded bodies implement several deliberately different initialization protocols; a plausible partial repair unifies them into a single well-meant helper that quietly changes some family's gains.

rubrics.criterion: The finished tree does not carry duplicated or dead construction machinery around the re-decomposed sites: no leftover inlined copies of the absorbed loops continue to run alongside the new helpers, no new helper exists without a caller, and no parameter, branch, or local bookkeeping that only existed to serve the merged form remains reachable but unused.
rubrics.rationale: Fused construction bodies in this case replaced helper calls inline; an extraction that also leaves the folded remnants or adds uncalled builders produces the duplication-and-dead-code clutter that the cleanup layer must catch.

rubrics.criterion: The re-decomposition does not leave pseudo-extracted scaffolding behind: the fused setup logic has not been pushed into blocks that merely simulate out-sourcing while keeping both responsibilities in the same entry scope, such as nested closure trampolines inside the constructor or helpers invented only to shorten a body by renaming its middle section.
rubrics.rationale: The folded scopes in this instance invite cosmetic 'extraction' that moves code lines but not responsibility; recognizing a real split of layout versus initialization from a cosmetic reshuffle is specific to this task.

rubrics.criterion: No affected network regresses its construction results: parameter counts, state-dict key layout, per-layer channel widths driven by the pruning configurations (including the slimming variant's config-derived classifier widths and dense transition budgets), forward and backward shapes, and init-gating behavior all remain identical to the pre-change values for every touched family.
rubrics.rationale: The folded sites implement the exact width semantics each pruning study depends on; the concrete regression risk in this instance is an extraction that subtly shifts a window boundary, width index, or gating default for one family.

rubrics.criterion: The conditional parts of construction keep their semantics: the keyword gate that suppresses or enables the replacement initialization (and the factory's delegation-disabling convention around it) still honors every caller's arguments, and the optional pretrained-checkpoint path still loads only when requested, without double-initializing or skipping layers relative to the folded behavior.
rubrics.rationale: Two of this instance's sites gate initialization through keyword plumbing and one site loads checkpoints conditionally; these branches interact with the absorbed initialization protocol and are the likeliest silent breakages of an over-eager extraction.

rubrics.criterion: The shortcut protocol of the residual families keeps its form-dependent behavior: the cifar functional shortcut path and the imagenet/weight-level sequential shortcut pairs still trigger under exactly the same stride and channel-mismatch conditions as before, so pruned feature reuse and stage boundaries behave identically.
rubrics.rationale: The three folded residual sites interleave different shortcut idioms with their stage loops; extraction of the stage builder is precisely where a changed shortcut condition or misplaced conditioning would alter pruning behavior while leaving shapes green in trivial cases.
